Author: Alok Kumar Verma
Bench: Ramesh Ranganathan, Alok Kumar Verma
 In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Writ Petition (Ms) No. 3845 of 2018

sentences.text:
Mehboob Qureshi and others ..........Petitioners  Vs.
State of Uttarakhand Through Secretary In The Department Of Local Bodies Dehradun And Others ...........
Respondents Present:-

Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Aditya Kumar Arya,
learned Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned Standing Counsel for the Nagar Nigam, Haldwani.

Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
On one flimsy excuse or the other, the order of this Court in WPPIL No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018 is being flouted by the respondents with impunity.

The said order obligated all illegal slaughter houses in the State of Uttarakhand to be sealed within 72 hours from the date of the order, and required the Secretary (Home) to ensure that no animal is slaughtered, on the streets or open spaces, forthwith.

The Division Bench also directed all Executive Officers of Local Self Governments, Municipal Corporations, Municipalities, Nagar Panchayats and other Panchayats to ensure that no animal is slaughtered in the public streets/public paths/roads and at open spaces, open to public gaze.

2. Pursuant to the said order dated 20.09.2018, the Haldwani slaughter house, and the other slaughter houses in the State, were all closed, evidently because they were not in compliance with the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The other direction, issued by the Division Bench in its order dated 20.09.2018, to ensure that no animal is slaughtered in streets, parks, roads and open spaces etc, has evidently not been complied with, since meat continues to be sold unabated in all hotels/restaurants in the State of Uttarakhand,
and continues to be consumed by the residents of this State.

sentences.text:
The respondents have not only violated the order passed by the Division Bench in WPPIL No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018, but also the earlier order of the Division Bench in WPPIL No.77 of 2010 dated 19.12.2011, whereby the State and its agencies were required to ensure that adequate number of slaughter houses were available in the areas coming under Municipalities, and other local authorities, within a period of three years.
4. At every stage of the hearing of this case, the Handwani Municipality has expressed some difficulty or the other in complying with the directions of the Division Bench in WPPIL No. 77 and 73 of 2011 dated 19.12.2011, and in WPPIL No. 152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018.

On a few occasions when the matter was listed, the Learned Counsel for the Municipality did not even choose to be present in Court forcing us to direct the Commissioner to be present in Court, along with the entire records, to enable effective adjudication of the lis.
5. Initially the Haldwani Municipality submitted an application to the Central Authorities seeking a license to establish a slaughter house to slaughter 55 Buffalos each day.

When the matter was listed,
before us thereafter, they complained that permission was not forthcoming; and that their repeated requests have been rejected on one ground or the other by the Central Authorities.

On the learned Counsel for the petitioner pointing out that the pre-existing slaughter house in Haldwani Municipality catered only to the slaughter of 15 to 20 Buffalos every day, and it was wholly unnecessary for the Haldwani Municipality to approach the Central Government and it would have sufficed for them to seek permission of the State Government to establish a slaughter house, for slaughter of less than 50 Buffalos every day, the Haldwani Municipality had, thereafter, made an application to the State Government.

6. Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand, had assured this Court that, in the light of the order of the Division Bench in WPPIL No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018, the application of the Haldwani Municipality would be processed with utmost expedition.

Today when the matter is called, the Haldwani Municipality complains that they have not yet been granted approval because the State Government insists that a No Objection Certificate be produced from the State Pollution Control Board; the State Pollution Control Board requires the Municipality to construct a pit for flow of animal blood from the carcasses therein; the cost of construction of such a pit would exceed Rs. 20 lacs for which a DPR is required to be prepared, and tenders called; the Municipality has prepared a DPR; and hearing of the writ petition be deferred by two months to enable them to comply with this condition stipulated by the State Pollution Control Board.
7.
The said order of the Division Bench dated 19.12.2011 required slaughter houses to be established before 18.12.2014.

While every possible excuse is being put forth, for not complying with the aforesaid orders of this Court, we see no reason to show any further indulgence in this regard, for the order of this Court in WPPIL NO. 77 of 2010 and 73 of 2010 dated 19.12.2011 obligated the State and its agencies to establish adequate number of slaughter houses within a period of three years which expired on 19.12.2014 nearly five years ago, and yet there is not a single legally complaint slaughter house establish in the State of Uttarakhand till date.

sentences.text: We consider it appropriate, in such circumstances, to direct that show cause notices be issued to the Secretary, Urban Development, State of Uttarakhand, the District Magistrate, Nainital, the Executive Officer, Nagar Palika Parishad, Nainital, the Nagar Nigam, Haldwani, represented by its Nagar Ayukth, and the Designated Officer, Food Safety and Standards, District Nainital, to show cause why suo-moto proceedings should not be initiated against them, under the Contempt of Courts Act, for their, prima facie, willful and deliberately violation of the aforesaid orders of this Court.

9. Let notices be issued to the Secretary, Urban Development, State of Uttarakhand; the District Magistrate, Nainital; the Executive Officer, Nagar Palika Parishad, Nainital; the Nagar Nigam,
Haldwani, represented by its Nagar Ayukth; and the Designated Officer, Food Safety and Standard,
District Nainital, by the Registry, through personal messenger; and proof of service be filed latest by 22.11.2019.

These officials shall be personally present in Court on 25.11.2019 at 10:15 A.M., and shall file an affidavit by that date showing cause why action should not be initiated against them, under the Contempt of Courts Act, for what appears to us, prima facie, to be willful and deliberate violation of the orders passed by this Court in WPPIL Nos. 77 and 73 of 2011 dated 19.12.2011, and in WPPIL No. 152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018. .

10. Post along with WPMS No. 3894 of 2018.
11.
The Commissioner, Haldwani Municipality is present in Court today.
He shall be present on 25.11.2019 also.
12. Let a certified copy of this order be supplied to the learned counsel for the parties, on payment of the prescribed charges, by 18.11.2019.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.) 16.11.2019
